solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Broken bone starts to fuse rapidly and heal, taking time

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each word is kept
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: first letters of these three words
to heal is to cure
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A doctor hopes a broken bone will knit together fast and heal, given enough time.
explanation.walkthrough: The time letter sits inside the word for heal: C-T-URE, after the three initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is the medical term for a crack or break in a bone, so the noun phrase matches exactly.

clue.text: Escape from loud match?

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a match is something that gives a light; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: Someone wants to get away from a noisy football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' reads as a sporting fixture, but here it is the thing you strike, which gives you a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking flight means running away, so flight is a noun for an escape from danger or captivity.

clue.text: Praise unusual aim

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its ordinary form, so these letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone receives praise for an unusual ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'aim' as a verb: the answer is a verb meaning to set your sights on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have ambitions and strive towards a goal, a close synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Abrupt beginning to teaching Gaelic language

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so just that one letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter
Erse is an old name for the Gaelic language of Scotland or Ireland

explanation.surface: A sudden start to Gaelic lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: Erse is a crossword favourite for Gaelic, especially Scottish or Irish Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Terse speech is brief to the point of curtness, which is the same as an abrupt manner.

clue.text: Wine boxes every one got

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: red is a type of wine
each means every one individually

explanation.surface: Each person was handed a boxed bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' looks like a noun for wine cartons, but it is a verb: the wine word wraps the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In the sense of arriving at a place, got and reached are interchangeable past-tense verbs, as in 'got home'.

clue.text: Married different relative

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
other means different

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an in-law of a different sort; the M for married is the usual genealogical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is a family member, a specific example of a relative by blood.

clue.text: Resolve us? Resolve us!

indicators.note: to resolve can mean to break into parts and recombine, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: both words taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: A question then an exclamation: shall we make up our minds? Yes, let's decide!
explanation.walkthrough: The repetition hides the split: the first two words are the letters, the repeated verb is the signal, and the last word defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The reflexive pronoun is the emphatic or object form of the first person plural, standing in for the plain pronoun.

clue.text: Doubtful, wavering atheist receiving note

indicators.note: something wavering is unsteady and shifting, so these letters move into a new order
to receive is to take in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A non-believer starts to waver, unsure of himself, after getting a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged unbeliever gives HESITAT, and N slips in before the final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hesitant is uncertain and holding back, so doubtful is a fair synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: Revived a show, perhaps, that’s old after intermission

blocks.note: an intermission is a break or rest
aged means old

explanation.surface: A theatre brings back an old production, the kind you watch with an interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the old piece behind the break piece. 'Intermission' fits the theatre picture but only means a pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a play on again is staging it a second time; 'perhaps' admits a show is only one example of what is restaged.

clue.text: Magnificent place in danger over tax, essentially

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept
lying over something on all sides covers it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: to imperil is to put at risk
central letter

explanation.surface: A grand estate is under threat from a tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' looks like a noun for the magnificent estate, but 'place in danger' is a single verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial means befitting an emperor, hence majestic and grand in scale.

clue.text: King is repeatedly in predicament

blocks.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
the word is written twice

explanation.surface: A monarch keeps finding himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: CR, for Carolus Rex (King Charles), is a standard crossword abbreviation for king; 'repeatedly' just doubles the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: A crisis is a time of serious difficulty, which is what being in a predicament amounts to.

clue.text: Gamble on a second classification

blocks.note: to gamble is to bet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter puts money on the second-ranked runner.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' just stacks one piece on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, used as a grade meaning second class in marking work.

clue.text: Speaker’s gruff command to scare away possible bringer of fortune

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what the listener hears, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: a gruff voice is hoarse
shoo is what you say to drive off a cat or bird

explanation.surface: A speaker barks a rough order to drive something off.
explanation.walkthrough: Said in a gruff voice, 'hoarse shoo' sounds like the lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseshoe nailed above a door is a traditional good-luck token, so 'possible' covers its being only superstition.

clue.text: Additional section of flex trails

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from something longer, so the letters lie inside the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An extension lead trails across the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A flex is the British word for an electric cable; the letters sit across its end and the start of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra and additional are straightforward synonyms, both meaning more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Employed American editor

blocks.note: US is short for American
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A US newspaper editor has a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Employed' suggests having a job, but here it means put to use.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to use it, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Primarily smiling Prince Harry tours Morecambe, getting round

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is kept
touring goes all the way round, so one piece encircles another

blocks.note: first letters of both words
Hal is the nickname of Prince Harry, the future Henry V, in Shakespeare
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian

explanation.surface: A grinning Prince Harry visits the seaside town of Morecambe and has put on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire resort but is the comedian Eric Morecambe; Harry gives Shakespeare's Prince Hal, which goes round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spherical is shaped like a ball, so it is round in every direction.

clue.text: Progress in a tango perhaps absorbing Victor

indicators.note: to absorb is to take in, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: a tango is one example of a dance, hence 'perhaps'
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dancer called Victor improves at the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tango' is also a NATO letter, but here it is just an example of a dance; Victor is the alphabet word.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance is to move forward or improve, a direct synonym of the verb progress.

clue.text: A new silk could be elegant

indicators.note: 'could be' hints at a possible alternative version, so the letters may be put in another order

blocks.note: all three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh piece of silk fabric might look refined.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the first three words is used; 'new' wants to be the signal but is part of the material.
explanation.definitionFit: Swans are a byword for graceful poise, so being like a swan suggests grace and refinement.

clue.text: Supplies for five important days in Rome

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
V is the Roman numeral for five
the Ides were key dates in the Roman calendar, the 13th or 15th of the month

explanation.surface: Rations for five big days in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supplies' looks like a noun for provisions, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide something is to furnish or make it available, the same as the verb supply.

clue.text: Paddle back alongside vessel for part of service

indicators.note: going back runs the opposite way, so the letters are written from end to start

blocks.note: to paddle a boat is to row it
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: Rowing back beside a boat, perhaps in a naval ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'service' both hint at the navy; the answer is the church sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is a religious service or the devotion offered during one, as in a place of worship.

clue.text: Picked up white bucket

indicators.note: to pick something up can mean to hear it, as on a radio, so sound matters here

blocks.note: pale means white or wan

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a white bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' fits a bucket literally, which disguises its role as hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is an old-fashioned word for a bucket, a container with a handle for carrying liquids.

clue.text: Lamps seen regularly in alcove

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, so alternate ones are kept

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Lights are spotted at intervals inside a recess.
explanation.walkthrough: Start from the second letter and take every other one across both words.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church, a large kind of alcove.

clue.text: Raffia’s made into things

indicators.note: something made is fashioned from raw material, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the word with its possessive s, seven letters

explanation.surface: Palm fibre is woven into all sorts of objects.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so the s counts as a letter. Raffia is a fibre from a palm used in weaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs can mean matters or concerns in general, as in 'how are things?' meaning 'how are your affairs?'

clue.text: Felt sorry for Greek character on special diet

indicators.note: something special is made to order, so these letters are arranged differently

blocks.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sympathised with a Greek man on a strict eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the Greek letter on top of the reworked diet letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity someone is to feel compassion at their misfortune, matching the past-tense phrase.

clue.text: Spend earnings retaining charm

indicators.note: to retain is to hold within, so the letters sit inside the surrounding words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone splashes their wages on a lucky trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' tempts as a noun, a lucky trinket, but it is the verb: to win affection.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear yourself to people is to win their fondness, which is what charming them does.

clue.text: At no point damage nerve

indicators.note: damage knocks something out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, five letters

explanation.surface: A warning: don't ever injure a nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Only two letters swap places: the V and the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Never means at no time whatsoever, so the adverbial phrase is a direct equivalent.

clue.text: In apartment, something that’s charged for rising prices

blocks.note: taken as written
a flat is the British word for an apartment
an ion is an electrically charged particle

explanation.surface: A tenant complains that the rent on the apartment keeps going up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests billing a tenant, but it means carrying an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflation is the economic term for a general increase in the cost of goods over time.

clue.text: Fragrance of a European capital for its inhabitants

blocks.note: taken as written
Roma is what Italians call Rome

explanation.surface: The smell of a European city as the locals know it.
explanation.walkthrough: The city is Rome, but in the local Italian form.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant distinctive smell, close in meaning to a fragrance or scent.

clue.text: Charge into court after police officer

blocks.note: in can mean into
DI is a Detective Inspector
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A suspect is charged and taken to court following a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the court letters behind the officer. DI, Detective Inspector, is a British police rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To indict is to formally accuse someone of a crime, the legal sense of the verb charge.

clue.text: Incite no criminal to produce a stimulant

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or wrong, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: both words taken as written, eight letters

explanation.surface: Advice not to encourage a lawbreaker to supply drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun, a lawbreaker, but it is an adjective signalling the shake-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the addictive substance in tobacco, which acts on the nervous system as a stimulant drug.

clue.text: Loosen edges of ladders’ supports

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its two ends, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: to ease a knot or grip is to loosen it
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone loosens the feet of ladders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supports' seems to belong with the ladders, but it stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Easels are wooden stands that hold up a painting or blackboard, so they are kinds of supports.

clue.text: I throw mud at Sicilian, say

blocks.note: taken as written
to throw mud is to defame someone

explanation.surface: A confession: I insult a man from Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throw mud at' is the idiom for blackening a reputation, not a literal throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is an island, so a Sicilian is one example of an island inhabitant, as 'say' signals.
